bull.b: The large recurring revenue base from instruments, accessories, and service provides meaningful visibility beyond one-time system sales. As the installed fleet and procedure volumes expand, repeat purchases can support durable growth, resilience, and operating leverage across future periods.

A growing installed base strengthens Intuitive Surgical’s ecosystem by expanding the future pool of procedures, recurring consumables, and service contracts. It also deepens customer familiarity with the platform and creates a durable foundation for adoption across specialties and care settings.

High operating margins and rapidly growing free cash flow demonstrate strong economics and substantial internal funding capacity. This combination can support continued research, product development, customer training, and strategic shareholder returns without depending heavily on external financing.

bear.b: Although revenue and earnings remain strong, slower growth than earlier periods may make it harder to sustain historical expansion rates. A decelerating trajectory can constrain operating leverage, reduce the pace of installed-base growth, and increase dependence on successful new products and indications.

Weak tender activity, local competition, and policy-driven pricing pressure create a durable headwind in China, while da Vinci 5 is not yet cleared there. Lower placements can limit installed-base expansion and defer the recurring procedure, instrument, and service revenue opportunity.

The extended-use program could improve customer economics and encourage adoption, but using instruments for more procedures may reduce instrument-and-accessory revenue per case. That creates a structural risk to the company’s recurring razor-and-blades model if utilization expands faster than replacement demand.
